title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: 5.1.3 Classical Tokenization
summary: ML models can't process raw text—they need structured units.
objectives: Understand what tokenization is and why it matters
Learn when to use sentence vs word tokenization

sections.title: What is Tokenization?
sections.body:
**Tokenization** = Breaking text into smaller units (tokens)

```
Visual:

Text: "Hello, world! How are you?"
         ↓ Tokenization
Tokens: ["Hello", ",", "world", "!", "How", "are", "you", "?"]
```

### Why Tokenization Matters

ML models can't process raw text—they need **structured units**.

```
Pipeline:
Raw Text → Tokenization → Vectorization → Model
"I love NLP" → ["I", "love", "NLP"] → [0.1, 0.8, 0.3] → Prediction
```

sections.title: 1 Whitespace Tokenization
sections.body:
### The Simplest Approach

Split on spaces!

```python
# Basic whitespace tokenization
text = "Hello world! How are you?"

# Method 1: split()
tokens = text.split()
print("Tokens:", tokens)
print("Count:", len(tokens))
```

### Problems with Whitespace Tokenization

```
Visual Problems:

1. Punctuation stuck to words:
   "world!" → Should be "world" and "!"

2. Contractions:
   "don't" → Is this 1 or 2 tokens?

3. Compound words:
   "New York" → Should be 1 or 2 tokens?
```

```python
# Demonstrate the problems
problematic_texts = [
    "Hello, world!",
    "I don't know",
    "New York City",
    "It's a $50.99 item"
]

for text in problematic_texts:
    tokens = text.split()
    print(f"Text: {text}")
    print(f"Tokens: {tokens}")
    print()
```

sections.title: 2 Rule-Based Tokenization
sections.body:
### Using Regular Expressions

Define rules for what counts as a token

```python
import re

def regex_tokenize(text):
    """
    Token pattern: word characters or punctuation
    \w+ = one or more word characters (letters, digits, underscore)
    [^\w\s] = anything that's not a word char or whitespace
    """
    pattern = r'\w+|[^\w\s]'
    tokens = re.findall(pattern, text)
    return tokens

# Test it
text = "Hello, world! How are you?"
tokens = regex_tokenize(text)
print("Tokens:", tokens)
print("Count:", len(tokens))
```

```python
# Test on problematic cases
test_cases = [
    "I don't know",
    "It's $50.99",
    "Email: user@example.com",
    "Visit https://example.com"
]

for text in test_cases:
    tokens = regex_tokenize(text)
    print(f"Text: {text}")
    print(f"Tokens: {tokens}")
    print()
```

### Advanced Regex Patterns

```python
def advanced_tokenize(text):
    """
    Handle:
    - Contractions (don't, it's)
    - Numbers with decimals (50.99)
    - Emails
    - Punctuation
    """
    pattern = r'''
        (?:[A-Z]\.)+              # Abbreviations (U.S.A.)
        |\$?\d+(?:\.\d+)?%?       # Numbers with optional $ and %
        |\w+(?:[-']\w+)*          # Words with optional hyphens/apostrophes
        |[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+(?:\.[\w-]+)+  # Emails
        |[^\w\s]                  # Single punctuation
    '''
    tokens = re.findall(pattern, text, re.VERBOSE)
    return tokens

# Test comprehensive cases
text = "I don't know! It's $50.99 at U.S.A. Email: test@example.com"
tokens = advanced_tokenize(text)
print("Tokens:", tokens)
```

sections.title: 3 NLTK Tokenization
sections.body:
### Word Tokenization

```python
import nltk

# Download required data (run once)
nltk.download('punkt', quiet=True)
nltk.download('punkt_tab', quiet=True)

from nltk.tokenize import word_tokenize

text = "Hello, world! How are you? I'm learning NLP."
tokens = word_tokenize(text)

print("Tokens:", tokens)
print("Count:", len(tokens))
```

### Comparing Different Tokenizers

```python
from nltk.tokenize import (
    word_tokenize,
    wordpunct_tokenize,
    TreebankWordTokenizer
)

text = "I don't know! It's $50.99."

# Whitespace
print("Whitespace:", text.split())

# word_tokenize (Penn Treebank style)
print("word_tokenize:", word_tokenize(text))

# wordpunct_tokenize (splits on punctuation)
print("wordpunct:", wordpunct_tokenize(text))

# TreebankWordTokenizer
tokenizer = TreebankWordTokenizer()
print("Treebank:", tokenizer.tokenize(text))
```

### Visual Comparison

```
Text: "I don't know! It's $50.99."

Whitespace:       ["I", "don't", "know!", "It's", "$50.99."]
word_tokenize:    ["I", "do", "n't", "know", "!", "It", "'s", "$", "50.99", "."]
wordpunct:        ["I", "don", "'", "t", "know", "!", "It", "'", "s", "$", "50", ".", "99", "."]
```

sections.title: 4 Sentence Tokenization
sections.body:
### Why Sentence Tokenization?

Some tasks need sentence-level processing:
- Summarization
- Translation
- Sentiment per sentence

```python
from nltk.tokenize import sent_tokenize

text = """
Hello! How are you? I'm learning NLP. 
It's amazing. Natural language is complex.
"""

sentences = sent_tokenize(text)
print("Number of sentences:", len(sentences))
print("\nSentences:")
for i, sent in enumerate(sentences, 1):
    print(f"{i}. {sent.strip()}")
```

### Edge Cases in Sentence Tokenization

```python
# Tricky cases
tricky_texts = [
    "Dr. Smith works at U.S.A. Inc. He likes it.",
    "The price is $19.99. Is that okay?",
    "What?! No way! Really?",
    "Email me at test@example.com. I'll reply soon."
]

for text in tricky_texts:
    sentences = sent_tokenize(text)
    print(f"Text: {text}")
    print(f"Sentences: {sentences}")
    print()
```

sections.title: 5 spaCy Tokenization
sections.body:
### Modern, Fast Tokenization

```python
import spacy

# Load English model
# If not installed: python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm
try:
    nlp = spacy.load('en_core_web_sm')
    
    text = "I don't know! It's $50.99 at U.S.A."
    doc = nlp(text)
    
    # Tokens
    tokens = [token.text for token in doc]
    print("Tokens:", tokens)
    
    # Token attributes
    print("\nToken details:")
    for token in doc:
        print(f"{token.text:12} | is_punct: {token.is_punct} | is_digit: {token.is_digit} | is_stop: {token.is_stop}")
        
except OSError:
    print("spaCy model not installed. Run: python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm")
```

### Sentence Segmentation with spaCy

```python
try:
    nlp = spacy.load('en_core_web_sm')
    
    text = "Dr. Smith works at U.S.A. Inc. He likes it. What about you?"
    doc = nlp(text)
    
    print("Sentences:")
    for i, sent in enumerate(doc.sents, 1):
        print(f"{i}. {sent.text}")
        
except OSError:
    print("spaCy model not installed")
```

sections.title: 6 Practical Comparison
sections.body:
### Speed Benchmark

```python
import time

# Sample text
text = """Natural language processing is a fascinating field. 
It combines linguistics and computer science. 
I'm excited to learn more about it!"""

# Repeat for timing
text = text * 100

def time_tokenizer(name, func, text):
    start = time.time()
    tokens = func(text)
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    return elapsed, len(tokens) if isinstance(tokens, list) else len(list(tokens))

# Test different tokenizers
results = []

# Whitespace
elapsed, count = time_tokenizer('Whitespace', lambda t: t.split(), text)
results.append(('Whitespace', elapsed, count))

# Regex
elapsed, count = time_tokenizer('Regex', regex_tokenize, text)
results.append(('Regex', elapsed, count))

# NLTK
elapsed, count = time_tokenizer('NLTK', word_tokenize, text)
results.append(('NLTK', elapsed, count))

# spaCy
try:
    nlp = spacy.load('en_core_web_sm')
    elapsed, count = time_tokenizer('spaCy', lambda t: [tok.text for tok in nlp(t)], text)
    results.append(('spaCy', elapsed, count))
except:
    pass

# Display results
print("Tokenization Benchmark:")
print("-" * 50)
for name, elapsed, count in results:
    print(f"{name:12} | Time: {elapsed:.4f}s | Tokens: {count}")
```

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.body:
### Tokenization Hierarchy

```
Document
   ├── Sentences (sentence tokenization)
   │      └── Words (word tokenization)
   │             └── Subwords (next lesson!)
   └── ...
```

### Best Practices

```
✓ DO:
  • Choose tokenizer based on task
  • Test on your specific data
  • Handle edge cases (URLs, emails, etc.)
  • Consider language-specific rules
  • Benchmark if speed matters

✗ DON'T:
  • Use whitespace for production
  • Ignore contractions
  • Over-split meaningful units
  • Assume one-size-fits-all
```

### When to Use What

- **Whitespace**: Quick prototypes only
- **Regex**: Custom rules, specific domains
- **NLTK**: Standard NLP tasks, research
- **spaCy**: Production systems, modern NLP
- **Subword** (next): Transformers, handling OOV

**Next**: Subword tokenization (BPE, WordPiece, SentencePiece)!
